dawarich.title: Phone GPS (Dawarich)
dawarich.privacy: Phone positions are only stored where they become part of a car trip. Other positions are discarded.

status.badKey: Dawarich rejected the API key. Check the server configuration.
status.unreachable: Dawarich could not be reached or returned an unsupported response.

dawarich.none: No identifiable trackers found recently. Type a tracker ID and press Enter.
dawarich.linkHint: New trips only. A tracker missing from the list can be typed in by its ID. Clear all trackers to switch off. The phone must follow the car; only one matching tracker is used per trip.
dawarich.backfillHint: Queues older trips up to now. Edited and already fused trips are skipped. Processing happens gradually in the background.
dawarich.queued: Backfill queued. Routes will update as trips are processed.

chargeHistory.title: Charge history
chargeHistory.subtitle: Every charge in the period under Filters, rebuilt from what the car reported while it charged. Open a session for its power curve, where it charged, and the distance and energy since the charge before. The kWh are the change in the car's own battery reading, not what the charger delivered.
chargeHistory.periodDesc: The days whose charge sessions are listed and totalled.
chargeHistory.locationUnavailable: Location was not reported for this session.
chargeHistory.noPowerData: No charging-power readings were recorded for this session.
chargeHistory.empty: No charge sessions are available yet.

cardDesc.sessions: The number of charging sessions in the chosen period, reconstructed from the charging state the car reported. A session still in progress counts too.
cardDesc.batteryEnergyGained: The rise in battery energy, added up over the sessions: the energy that reached the battery, which is less than what the charger delivered. Shown only when the battery's capacity is known: on a BEV from the car, on a plug-in hybrid once the pack's real capacity is configured.
cardDesc.timeCharging: The time from the start to the end of charging, added up over the finished sessions. A session still in progress counts once it ends.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.cardWithoutData: Hidden until your car reports this

cardDesc.location: The car's last known location on a small map. Click the map or the expand button to open the full map, or the directions button for map options.
cardDesc.fuelLevel: Shows the current fuel tank level as a percentage.
cardDesc.fuelRange: Estimated remaining driving range based on the current fuel level.
cardDesc.evBattery: State of charge as a percentage. On a PHEV or BEV this is your electric range gauge. On an HEV the hybrid battery is small and managed automatically by the car, so the exact value is less meaningful day-to-day.
cardDesc.electricRange: Distance the car estimates it can still drive on electricity alone, from the current state of charge. Only relevant for PHEV and BEV. Cold weather and motorway speeds shorten it. Some cars never report a range of zero, so an empty battery can keep showing the last few kilometres the car sent.
cardDesc.charging: Indicates whether the car is currently charging.
cardDesc.odometer: Total distance the car has traveled since manufacture.
cardDesc.battery12v: Voltage of the 12V auxiliary battery that powers the car's electronics.
cardDesc.doors: Lock status and open or closed state of all doors, bonnet and boot.
cardDesc.windows: Open or closed status of all four windows.
cardDesc.sunRoof: Whether the sunroof is currently open or closed.
cardDesc.climate: Climate control status including temperature and seat heating settings.
cardDesc.hvBattery: High-voltage battery details: state of charge, voltage, current and live power flow. On a PHEV or BEV it also shows the charge target and the charge current limit, which you can change. On an HEV it lets you see regeneration and motor-assist activity in real time. kWh figures appear only when the pack's real capacity is configured, because the gateway assumes an EV-sized pack for every car.
cardDesc.findMyCar: Activate the horn and lights to help locate your car in a parking area.
cardDesc.lights: On or off status of high beam, low beam and sidelights.
cardDesc.efficiencyDistance: Total distance driven so far today.
cardDesc.efficiencyEnergy: What the car has used since midnight. On a BEV or PHEV that is electrical energy through the high-voltage battery, in kilowatt-hours. On an HEV the same counter carries the trip computer's fuel total instead, so it is shown in litres.
cardDesc.efficiencyCharge: Distance driven since the last charge session.
cardDesc.efficiencySinceCharge: Energy used per distance since the last charge, in {energyPerDistance}, where {energyBetter}. It comes from the battery's own since-last-charge counters, which start again at every charge. Only relevant for PHEV and BEV.
cardDesc.efficiencyRatio: How much the car used for the distance driven today. On a BEV or PHEV that is {energyPerDistance}, where {energyBetter}, and it translates directly to electricity cost per {distance}. On an HEV it is fuel consumption in {fuelConsumption}, where {fuelBetter}: motorway driving gives a better figure than short stop-start trips from cold. When no driving data is available yet, HEV and PHEV fall back to estimated fuel economy ({distancePerPercent}) derived from the car's own range computer, where higher is more efficient.
cardDesc.speed: Current vehicle speed as reported by the gateway.
cardDesc.topSpeed: Highest speed recorded across all GPS points in the most recent completed trip.
cardDesc.activeTrip: Distance covered in the current trip while active, or the distance of the last completed trip when parked.
cardDesc.remainingCharge: Estimated minutes remaining until the battery reaches the configured charge limit. Only relevant for PHEV and BEV while charging.
cardDesc.chargingSession: Live onboard-charger data: AC power (single or three-phase), cable lock status, charging type, and when the last charge started and ended. Only relevant for PHEV and BEV.
cardDesc.batteryHeating: High-voltage battery pre-heating status and schedule. Warming the battery before a charge session improves charging speed in cold weather. Only relevant for PHEV and BEV.
cardDesc.maintenance: Upcoming and overdue maintenance items based on the service intervals you define. Click through to the Maintenance page to add items or log a completed service.
cardDesc.rdw: The APK expiry date and the days left, open recalls and the WAM insurance, as the RDW has them on record for the car's Dutch plate. Click for each recall's risk and repair.
cardDesc.climateSchedule: When a climate schedule warms or cools the car next

dashboard.subtitle: What the car last reported. A parked car only checks in now and then, so the menu shows when these readings were recorded, and Refresh asks the car for fresh ones. Tap a tyre pressure, or the charge or fuel level on the car, for its history, and the (i) on a card for what it shows. Press and hold a card, or use Edit layout, to move, hide or show cards. Which cards appear follows the car's type, which you can set by hand under Settings > Vehicle.

cardDesc.distanceInRange: Distance the car counted over the selected period, from its own day counter, so it matches the energy used. A car that reports no such counter gets the total of its trips instead.
cardDesc.avgTripLength: Average distance per trip in the selected period.
cardDesc.periodEnergy: Energy the car took from its high-voltage battery over the selected period, as its own counter reports it. What the battery loses while the car is parked counts too.
cardDesc.periodFuel: Fuel burned over the selected period, from the trip computer's own counter.
cardDesc.periodEfficiency: What the car used per distance over the selected period: the energy (or fuel) it counted, divided by the distance it counted on the same days. Lower is better. Standby losses while parked count too, so a car that mostly stands still reads higher. Shown once the period holds at least {min} of driving.
cardDesc.climateUsage: Percentage of recorded snapshots during which remote climate preconditioning was active. Does not reflect in-car A/C usage while driving.
cardDesc.commutePattern: The hour of day with the most trip starts in the selected period - your most common time to drive.
cardDesc.batteryVoltageTrend: Change in average 12V battery voltage from the start to the end of the selected period. Shows current voltage when less than two days of data are available.
cardDesc.parkingLocations: Number of distinct parking spots used across all trips in the selected period, based on rounded GPS coordinates.
cardDesc.electricShare: Estimated share of today's driving on electric power, derived from the distance since the last charge versus the total distance today. Only meaningful for PHEV, where the battery can be charged from the grid.
cardDesc.avgSpeed: Average moving speed across all recorded GPS points in the selected period, excluding stopped moments.

chartDesc.evChart: Daily average EV battery state-of-charge over the selected period.
chartDesc.tyreChart: Daily average tyre pressure per wheel over the selected period. Typical passenger-car range is {low} – {high} {unit}.
chartDesc.hybridSocChart: Daily average EV battery and fuel level over the selected period. Lets you compare how both energy sources change together.
chartDesc.dailyKwhChart: The bars are the kWh taken from the battery per day, week or month, as the car's own counter reports it, standby losses while parked included. A finished day counts the peak of its counter; today counts only the increase since midnight, or since the last counter reset. The line is the efficiency over the same days, in {unit}, against the right-hand axis; a point with less than {min} of driving has none.
chartDesc.dailyFuelChart: The bars are the fuel burned per day, week or month, from the trip computer's own counter. A finished day counts the peak of its counter; today counts only the increase since midnight, or since the last counter reset. The line is the consumption over the same days, in {unit}, against the right-hand axis; a point with less than {min} of driving has none.
chartDesc.temperatureChart: What the car used per distance, in {unit}, on the days of the selected period grouped by their average outside temperature, coldest on the left. Lower is better. It shows how much more the car takes in the cold. A band whose days hold less than {min} of driving is left out.

statistics.periodDesc: The days the statistics cover. Longer periods are charted per week, and per month beyond a year.

months.title: Per month
months.needsLongerPeriod: Shown for a period of more than one month

statistics.subtitle: Figures for the period under Filters, worked out from the trips and readings the car reported. Charts show a point per day up to about three months, per week up to a year and per month beyond, and a period over a month adds a table per month. The (i) on a card says how its figure is worked out. Press and hold a card, or use Edit layout, to move or hide cards.

directions.mapApp: Open in a compatible map app (geo: link)
directions.copyFailed: Could not copy automatically. Select and copy the coordinates below.
directions.lastKnownUpdated: Last known location. Vehicle updated {time}; the location may be older.
directions.lastKnownUnknown: Last known location. Its age is unknown.
directions.moving: The car may be moving. Directions are unavailable while it appears to be on a trip.
directions.unavailable: Directions unavailable: the car's location is unknown.
directions.shareNotice: Opening a map shares these coordinates with that service or app.

vehicle.gatewaySignedOutHint: The gateway cannot sign in to the MG account, so no new data arrives from the car. It tries again every 15 minutes.

diagram.infoTyreDesc: Colour-coded dots at each wheel corner show the current pressure. Green means healthy ({good} – {high} {unit}), orange means low ({low} – {good} {unit}) and red means critically low (< {low} {unit}) or over-inflated (> {high} {unit}).
diagram.infoDoorsDesc: A lock-open icon appears over any door, the bonnet or the boot that is currently open.
diagram.infoLightsDesc: Light beam shapes are drawn when high beam, low beam or sidelights are active.
diagram.infoLevelDesc: When data is available, the fuel level percentage appears at the front and the EV battery percentage appears at the rear of the diagram. Tap either one, or a tyre's pressure, to see its last 30 days.
diagram.infoChargingDesc: A cable is shown below the battery indicator when the charger is connected. When actively charging, the cable animates with flowing dashes to show energy entering the car.

control.findMyCarConfirm: This will activate the horn and lights to help locate your car. Continue?
control.plugInFirst: Plug the car in to start charging.
control.scheduleCarTime: Times are in the car's own time zone.
control.rejected: The car did not carry out the command

trips.title: Trip history
trips.periodDesc: Filters trips shown on the map and in the list
trips.heatmapDesc: Shows how often each road was driven, measured by distance rather than by time spent standing on it
trips.routeOutlineDesc: Adds a dark border to route lines for better contrast
trips.snapToRoadsDesc: Draw the selected trip along the roads OpenStreetMap says it was driven on, instead of straight between GPS fixes.
trips.speedOverlayDesc: Visible when a single trip is selected
trips.speedLimitOverlayDesc: Colour the selected trip by what OpenStreetMap says was signposted along it.
trips.speedLimitOverSummary: {distance} over the limit ({pct}%), up to {speed} above
trips.speedLimitCoverage: Limits known for {pct}% of the trip
trips.speedLimitUnmapped: No speed limits mapped along this trip
trips.speedLimitTolerance: Counted as over only past {speed} above the limit. Limits that only apply at certain times, such as a motorway signed lower by day, are not in the data.
trips.chargingStationsDesc: Shows charging stations near your position.
trips.chargingPowerDesc: Filter stations by their available charging power
trips.fuelStationsDesc: Shows fuel stations near your position.
trips.phoneGpsDesc: Adds the stretches a phone recorded (through Dawarich or the app) to the trips, drawn dotted. Off, the map shows only what the car recorded itself.
trips.serviceAreasDesc: Shows motorway service areas and rest stops near your position.
trips.speedCamerasDesc: Shows speed cameras mapped in OpenStreetMap near your position. Some countries restrict warning a driver about camera positions while driving.
trips.fuelBrandFilterDesc: Show only selected fuel station brands. Applies once the fuel stations layer is on.
trips.fuelBrandNoneLoaded: No brands found yet. Pan the map to load stations.
trips.fuelTypeFilterDesc: Show only stations selling the selected fuels. Stations that do not list their fuels stay visible.
trips.subtitle: Every trip in the period under Filters, with a heatmap of the roads you drive most. Pick a trip in the list or on the map to see its route along the roads it took. The buttons on the map centre it on the car and choose what it draws, such as speed colours, speed limits, and charging or fuel stations. Dotted stretches were recorded by a phone rather than the car, and the pencil on a selected trip fixes a route the car got wrong.

install.title: Install GarageStack
install.description: Add GarageStack to your home screen for the best experience.
install.featureQuickStart: Opens in a tap from your home screen

push.permissionDenied: Permission denied, allow notifications in your browser settings
push.subscribeFailed: Could not register for push notifications. Check that the server is reachable, then try again.
push.enableDesc: Alerts arrive as system notifications, even while GarageStack is closed.
push.needsHttps: Push notifications need GarageStack on an https:// address. Browsers do not allow them on a plain http:// address other than localhost.

updates.availableLabel: GarageStack v{version} is available: read what changed

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.typeFilterDesc: Choose which notification types this device shows and gets pushed. The weekly and monthly summaries are off until you switch them on, and come only to a device with push on.
notifications.scopeDesc: Choose which car the list below is for. A type switched off for all cars stays off for every car.

auth.subtitle: Sign in to continue
auth.accessDenied: This account is not allowed to use GarageStack
auth.ssoFailed: Single sign-on failed, please try again
auth.noSignInMethod: No sign-in method is configured. Set a password login or an OIDC provider.
auth.apiUnreachable: Could not reach the API. It may still be starting.

theme.title: Appearance
theme.label: Theme
theme.desc: System follows the light or dark setting of this device.

language.title: Language
language.desc: The language GarageStack is shown in. Push notifications use the language set on the server.

carColor.title: Car colour
carColor.desc: How the car is drawn on the dashboard and the map.

phoneGps.label: Record GPS during drives
phoneGps.desc: Sends this phone's location to GarageStack while the app is open on screen, to fill in the gaps between the car's own positions in its trips. Only while GarageStack is in front: a navigation app on top stops it. Positions are kept 30 days.
phoneGps.needsScreen: Needs the screen kept on, so the app stays on screen during the drive.
phoneGps.denied: Location access is blocked for GarageStack. Allow it in the phone's settings, then switch this on again.

keepScreenOn.label: Keep the screen on
keepScreenOn.desc: Stops the screen from dimming or locking while the app is open, for a phone in a holder or a tablet on the wall. Uses more battery.

dashboard.cardInfoIconsDesc: Adds a button beside each page's title, and to each dashboard and statistics card, that explains what it shows.
dashboard.mapBackdropDesc: Shows the car's map across the whole dashboard, with the cards over it and the car parked where the location card was. Phones keep the location card.

map.placeNamesDesc: Name trips after the cities they ran between and show the street the car is parked in. Off lists trips by date and sends no coordinates to the geocoder.
map.colorfulDesc: Show every map in full colour. Off matches the maps to the dark or light theme.

vehicleType.title: Vehicle type
vehicleType.desc: The gateway reports {type}. Choose another type only if that is wrong: the dashboard cards, notifications and units on offer follow it.
vehicleType.notDetected: Not detected yet: the gateway reports it once it runs. Until then, choose the type here.

vehicleSettings.title: Settings for {car}
vehicleSettings.desc: This car's own battery size, tyre pressures and warning levels. Leave a field empty for the server's default, shown greyed out. The dashboard colours and the notifications follow them.

licensePlate.title: Licence plate
licensePlate.desc: The car's Dutch licence plate, for the APK date, recalls and insurance the RDW has on record. Only the plate is sent to the RDW.
licensePlate.label: Licence plate
licensePlate.saved: Saved and looked up at the RDW.

powerTailgate.label: Power tailgate
powerTailgate.desc: Switch this on if the car's boot opens and closes by itself. The Doors card can then open and close it, instead of only unlocking it. It starts on when the car reports a power tailgate. A car without a power tailgate refuses the command.

commutePlaces.title: Home and work
commutePlaces.desc: Trips between home and a work place are marked as commutes, and a place can notify you when the car arrives or leaves. In the trip log, a trip's start or end can be set as one too.

units.title: Language, region and units
units.regionDesc: Sets the date order, and the clock and units left on automatic.
units.clockDesc: How times of day are written.
units.currencyDesc: What maintenance costs are shown in. Changing it relabels the amounts; it does not convert them.
units.distanceDesc: Used for distances, the odometer and speed.
units.temperatureDesc: Used for the climate control and its schedules.
units.pressureDesc: Used for the tyre readings and their warning limits.
units.fuelConsumptionDesc: Used for fuel economy. Fuel used is counted in the same gallon.

apiTokens.title: API tokens
apiTokens.desc: Let a script, a dashboard or a watch read GarageStack's data without signing in. A token reads as your account and can only read: it cannot send commands or change anything. Send it as the header "Authorization: Bearer" followed by the token.
apiTokens.copyNow: Copy this token now: it is not shown again.

calendarFeed.title: Calendar feed
calendarFeed.desc: Subscribe to the APK expiry date, maintenance due dates and the next two weeks of climate schedules in any calendar app. The link opens this calendar and nothing else, but anyone who has it can read those dates.
calendarFeed.copyNow: Copy this link now: it is not shown again. Your calendar app fetches it by itself every few hours.
calendarFeed.confirmReplace: Replace? The old link stops working

export.title: Your data
export.desc: Everything GarageStack keeps, in one zip: per car its trips, maintenance, schedules, places and every telemetry reading, and your notifications and settings. Telemetry comes as a CSV file a spreadsheet opens, the rest as JSON. A big history takes a moment to gather.

tripLogExport.title: Trip log
tripLogExport.desc: A month or a year of trips as a spreadsheet, with the addresses and odometer readings a tax trip log (such as the Dutch rittenregistratie) asks for. Hidden trips are left out. Addresses not looked up yet are looked up first, which can take a while for a whole year.
tripLogExport.lookingUp: Looking up addresses: {n} trip to go | Looking up addresses: {n} trips to go

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.desc: For a bug report: the version, which parts are switched on and healthy, per car its model and type, the last 7 days of readings, and the warnings and errors of the last 7 days from the logs. VINs, licence plates, positions, email and IP addresses and web addresses are taken out, and trips, places and settings are left out. Look it over before you share it.

demo.banner: Demo mode - displaying sample data only
demo.failed: The demo car did not take that change. Try again.

tripLog.title: Trip log
tripLog.subtitle: Record what each trip was for, with the addresses and odometer readings a tax trip log asks for, and export it as a spreadsheet under Settings > Data & API. Trips appear here a few minutes after the car parks. Trips between home and work are marked as commutes: set the places under Settings > Vehicle > Home and work, or from a trip's start or end.
tripLog.classifyAll: {n} trip ({distance}) has no purpose yet. Mark it as: | {n} trips ({distance}) have no purpose yet. Mark them all as:

summary.label: Driving in this period
summary.open: Show driving time, average and longest trip, and average speed

cardDesc.allTrips: The distance driven over every trip in this period, with the number of trips in brackets. Hidden trips are left out. A trip's distance comes from the odometer, or from its GPS fixes when the car reported no odometer readings.
cardDesc.business: The distance of the trips marked as business, with the number of trips in brackets and their share of the period's distance below.
cardDesc.commute: The distance of the trips marked as commute, with the number of trips in brackets and their share of the period's distance below. Once home and work are set under Settings > Vehicle > Home and work, trips between them are marked as commutes automatically.
cardDesc.private: The distance of the trips marked as private, with the number of trips in brackets and their share of the period's distance below.
cardDesc.unclassified: The distance of the trips that have no purpose yet. Choose a purpose for each trip in the list, or mark them all at once with the buttons below these figures.
cardDesc.drivingTime: The time from departure to arrival, added up over every trip in this period. Stops in traffic count; the time parked between trips does not.
cardDesc.averageTrip: The period's distance divided by the number of trips.
cardDesc.longestTrip: The distance of the longest single trip in this period.
cardDesc.averageSpeed: The period's distance divided by the driving time, so stops in traffic and at lights lower it. A trip's own average speed in its details uses the speeds the car reported while moving instead.
cardDesc.fuelUsed: The fuel the car's trip computer counted over the trips in this period. Trips it sent no readings for are left out.
cardDesc.consumption: The fuel used over the distance of the same trips. Lower is better. Shown once those trips cover at least {min}.

detail.title: Trip details
detail.routeUnavailable: The route could not be loaded, so the map joins the ends with a straight line.
detail.averageSpeedHint: The mean of the speeds the car reported while moving
detail.fuelUsedHint: What the car's trip computer counted from leaving until it had parked
detail.consumptionHint: The fuel used over the trip's distance. Left out on a trip shorter than 1 km, where it is mostly rounding.

tripLog.odometer: Odometer at the start and end of the trip
tripLog.distanceFromGps: Distance along the GPS fixes; the car reported no odometer readings for this trip
tripLog.placesOff: Place names are switched off, so addresses show as coordinates. Switch them on under Settings > Map.
tripLog.empty: No saved trips in this period.

gpx.hint: Save the route as a GPX file, for a route planner, a sports app or geotagging photos
gpx.name: {date}: {from} to {to}

places.title: Home and work
places.intro: Trips between home and a work place are marked as commutes, including trips already in the log. Trips you classified yourself stay as they are.
places.empty: No home or work set yet.
places.homeTaken: This car already has a home. To move it, edit that place.
places.label: Name (optional)
places.mapHint: Click the map or drag the pin to where the car parks.
places.radiusHint: A trip ending within this distance of the pin counts as ending here.
places.notifyHint: A notification when the car parks here, and when it drives away. Each device can still switch these types off under Settings > Notifications.
places.removeConfirm: Remove this place? Trips it marked as commutes go back to unclassified.
places.marked: {n} trip marked as commute. | {n} trips marked as commute.
places.cleared: {n} trip no longer marked as commute. | {n} trips no longer marked as commute.
places.automaticHint: Marked as commute because the trip runs between home and work. Choose another purpose to override it.

tripLog.hideHint: Leave this trip out of the map, the statistics, the dashboard and these totals, for a positioning glitch. It stays listed under the hidden trips.
tripLog.joinNextHint: Joins this trip with the one after it, for a drive a short stop such as a fuel station split in two. You can undo it from the joined trip.
tripLog.unjoinHint: Puts back the two trips this one was joined from, as they were before the join. Changes made to this trip since are lost.

filter.periodDesc: The month, or the whole year, whose trips are listed and totalled.
filter.hiddenDesc: Hidden trips count nowhere. List them to show one again.

tripLog.showHidden: Show hidden trip | Show {n} hidden trips
tripLog.editedHint: The route was edited by hand. The distance still comes from the odometer.

tripEdit.title: Edit route
tripEdit.notFound: This trip cannot be edited. Only saved trips can be, a few minutes after the car parks.
tripEdit.suggestion: This trip probably started where the car was parked before it, which the car did not report. Start it there?
tripEdit.odometerNote: Editing the route changes the map and the addresses. The trip log keeps the distance the odometer counted.

hint.start: Tap the map where the trip started, or drag the green marker.
hint.end: Tap the map where the trip ended, or drag the red marker.
hint.points: Tap the map to add a point, or tap a point to select it.

tripEdit.pointLimit: This route has as many points as it can hold. Remove one to add another.
tripEdit.leaveConfirm: Leave without saving? The changes to this route will be lost.
tripEdit.noPreviousStop: No parking spot is known before this trip.
tripEdit.atPreviousStop: The trip already starts at the previous parking spot.
tripEdit.noNextStop: No parking spot is known after this trip.
tripEdit.atNextStop: The trip already ends at the next parking spot.
tripEdit.resetHint: Back to the route as the car recorded it. Save to keep it.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.subtitle: Keep the car's service items, each with a distance interval, a time interval or both, whichever comes first. An item is due soon at 90 % of its interval, and a notification comes then and once it is overdue. Logging a service starts its interval again, and its cost adds up at the top.
maintenance.deleteConfirm: Delete this maintenance item and its service history?
maintenance.empty: No maintenance items yet. Add one to start tracking service intervals.
maintenance.confirmDeleteLogEntryLabel: Tap again to delete this entry

form.name: Name
form.intervalHint: Set at least one interval. When both are set, the item is due whichever comes first.
form.lastServiceHint: Optional. Leave empty if this hasn't been serviced yet.
form.validationIntervalRequired: Set at least one interval (distance or time)

costs.hint: What the services you logged with a cost add up to, by the year they were done.

dashboard.allOk: All maintenance items are up to date

climateSchedules.title: Climate schedules
climateSchedules.subtitle: Warm or cool the car before you leave. Schedules run on the GarageStack server, so your phone can stay off. A schedule can run only on cold or warm days, going by the car's outside temperature. Each run sends a notification saying whether the car started climate, and a run the server finds more than 10 minutes late is skipped.
climateSchedules.empty: No schedules yet. Add one to have the car ready when you leave.

dashboard.label: Climate on
dashboard.add: Add a schedule to warm the car before you leave

form.name: Name (optional)
form.onceHint: No day chosen: runs once, then switches itself off.
form.onlyColdOrHot: Only when it is cold or hot
form.onlyColdOrHotDesc: Skips mild days, going by the car's outside temperature from the last 3 hours. Without a recent reading it runs anyway.
form.timingHint: Starts within a minute of the set time. The car takes up to 30 seconds per setting, so seat heating and the defroster follow shortly after.
form.zoneHint: Runs on {zone} time, where this schedule was made.
form.validationCondition: Enter at least one outside temperature.

errors.unauthorized: Your session has ended. Sign in again.
errors.conflict: That cannot be done right now.
errors.rateLimited: Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.
errors.server: Something went wrong on the server. Try again later.
errors.offline: GarageStack cannot be reached. Check your connection and try again.

dawarich.disabled: Dawarich is not configured on this server.
dawarich.invalidTrackers: Choose at most 10 distinct tracker identifiers, each up to 200 characters.
dawarich.invalidFrom: Choose a date between 2000 and today.
dawarich.notLinked: Save at least one linked tracker before backfilling.

csrf.originNotAllowed: This address is not allowed. Set CORS_ORIGIN to the address you open GarageStack on.

vehicle.accountUnknown: The car has not reported its MG account yet. Try again once it has sent data.

command.invalidValue: The car does not accept this value.
command.unsupported: This car does not support this command.

maintenance.nameTooLong: The name can be at most 200 characters.
maintenance.notesTooLong: The notes can be at most 1000 characters.
maintenance.intervalRequired: Set at least one interval (distance or time)
maintenance.intervalKmOutOfRange: The distance interval is outside the range GarageStack accepts.
maintenance.intervalMonthsOutOfRange: The time interval must be between 1 and 120 months.
maintenance.serviceDateInFuture: The service date cannot be in the future.
maintenance.odometerNegative: The odometer reading cannot be negative.
maintenance.costOutOfRange: The cost must be between 0 and 1,000,000, in cents at most.
